answer: In Proof of Agent, continuous identity verification binds each claimed node to a Wesolowski VDF: generating its proof requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, while verification checks the resulting commitment efficiently. Simulating multiple identities cannot parallelize any chain across GPUs, because each squaring depends on the preceding result; every clone therefore consumes real elapsed time, imposing a physical bottleneck against Sybil attacks. No island, zenith, or karst node gains a computational shortcut.
